title: Rhode Island Sues Meta in First US State Lawsuit Over Scam Ads

tickers.name: Meta Platforms, Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
A complaint filed by Rhode Island officials alleges that Meta enabled the proliferation of fraudulent advertisements through the use of AI-driven optimization tools. The legal action claims the company's technology helped scammers create fraudulent ads and that Meta sometimes charged suspected fraudsters extra fees rather than blocking their accounts. Internal estimates cited in the suit indicate 15 billion higher-risk scam ads are displayed daily, with projected 2024 revenue from scams and banned advertisements reaching approximately $16 billion.

The lawsuit identifies more than 2,000 active versions of a single advertisement claiming a 45 day cure for Alzheimer's disease. It further alleges that certain fraudulent advertisers have spent more on Meta's ad platforms over several years than established multinational corporations such as Walmart or Pfizer. Rhode Island is the first US state to bring a lawsuit against the company specifically over scam advertising.

selectedTweets.text:
HOLY MOLY. Reuters reports that Rhode Island has become the first US state to sue Meta over scam advertising, alleging Meta's own AI tools helped scammers create and optimize fraudulent ads, while suspected fraudsters were sometimes charged extra instead of being blocked.

The lawsuit cites internal estimates of 15 BILLION higher-risk scam ads shown daily and roughly $16 billion in projected 2024 revenue from scams and banned ads.

It also cites 2,000+ active versions of one ad promising to reverse Alzheimer's in 45 days, and alleges some scam advertisers spent more on Meta ads over several years than Walmart or Pfizer.
